title: On zero-sum Ramsey numbers of cycles and wheels
summary: For an integer $q\ge 2$ and a graph $F$ with $q\mid e(F)$, let $R(F,\Z_q)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every edge-labeling $w\colon E(K_n)\to \Z_q$ contains a copy of $F$ whose edge-label sum is zero in $\Z_q$. Write $C_{qk}$ for the cycle on $qk$ vertices. We prove that $R(C_{qk},\Z_q)\le \max\{R(C_{2q},\Z_q),qk+q-1\}$ via an insertion argument rooted in the classic Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem. Combined with Pikhurko's result, we obtain $R(C_{qk},\Z_q)\le \max\{35q^2,qk+q-1\}$ for every $q\ge 3$. We also show that $R(C_{qk},\Z_q)\ge qk+q-1$ for odd $q\ge 3$. Hence, for every fixed odd…
